CHRONOS·NEXUS

Jolotundo Observatory · −7.609444° +112.595556° · IERS 2010 · IAU 2000/2006
Torus: major angle = seconds within the minute of each time scale; tube angle = fractional second. Bead separation equals the true inter-scale offsets (e.g. TT−UTC = 69.184 s). Core: Earth rotating at the Earth Rotation Angle (ERA). Drag to rotate; double-tap to reset.

DEVICE CLOCK CALIBRATION

Displayed to the microsecond; absolute accuracy equals that of the device clock (typically ±10–100 ms via NTP). Enter the offset relative to a trusted time reference.
Nutation exaggeration×8000
Cyan: past 9.4 yr, magenta: next 9.4 yr of the CIP track about the mean pole (IAU 2000_R06 nutation, 6-day sampling). True amplitudes: Δψ ≈ 17.2″, Δε ≈ 9.2″ (18.6-yr term). Drag to orbit.
POLAR MOTION · x (right), y (up) from the EOP series
IERS Conventions (2010) Tables 5.2a/b/d/e and 5.3a/b: X, Y, s, Δψ, Δε and complementary terms of the equation of the equinoxes (IAU 2006/2000A_R06).

ERROR BUDGET

Display resolution (1 µs) is not accuracy. Values are 1σ-class estimates for this implementation.
UTC, absolute epoch±10–100 ms
Device clock disciplined via NTP; reducible to ~1–10 ms with the offset calibration against a trusted reference. performance.now() is quantised (5 µs–1 ms, browser-dependent). Sub-millisecond absolute time requires GNSS/PPS hardware.
TAI, TT, TCG offsetsexact
TAI−UTC from the integer leap-second table (37 s since 2017-01-01; assumes no later leap second, cf. IERS Bulletin C). TT−TAI = 32.184 s. TCG−TT by the IAU 2000 L_G definition.
TDB, TCB~ns level
HF2002 series (Harada & Fukushima), geocentric. The topocentric diurnal term (≲ 2 µs) is omitted. Not independently validated in this build.
UT1−UTC, C04 epochs≲ 0.04 ms
IERS 20C04 final, natural cubic spline of daily values. Sub-daily ocean-tide and libration terms (IERS Conventions 2010, Ch. 8) are not applied: order 10–100 µs.
UT1−UTC, Bulletin A epochshorizon-dependent
Rapid values ≈ 0.02–0.03 ms; predictions degrade as 0.25 ms·h^0.75 (see live regime panel).
ERA= UT1 limit
Exact function of UT1 (IAU 2000 definition); inherits the UT1 uncertainty.
CIP X, Y and CIO locator s≲ 1 µas
IAU 2006/2000A_R06 series (IERS Conventions 2010, Tables 5.2a/b/d), checked against SOFA reference vectors. Physical model limit ~0.1–0.3 mas (unmodelled free core nutation). Celestial pole offsets dX, dY are added to the displayed X, Y and propagate to GAST and EO.
Δψ, Δε≲ 1.5 µas
Differences against the IAU 2000A reference are consistent with the R06 adjustments.
GMST, GASTUT1-limited
Arithmetic ≲ 0.1 µs of sidereal time; 1 ms of UT1 error maps to 1.0027 ms. GAST includes the celestial pole offset via EE (dX·cos ε_A / sin ε₀); dX, dY are tabulated to MJD 61291 and held constant afterwards (free core nutation is not predicted), so the offset term can drift by a few tenths of a mas.
LMST, LAST+ ≲ 0.3 ms
The station vector is rotated ITRS→TIRS with polar motion and s′ (live value in the EARTH panel). Coordinates are quantised to 10⁻⁶° (≈ 0.24 ms), height assumed 0, deflection of the vertical ignored. Station displacements (solid Earth, loading; ≲ 0.1 ms) are not applied.
Polar motion, LODC04 level
Daily series, no sub-daily tidal model (sub-mas). Bulletin A values beyond the last observed epoch are predictions.
3D nutation viewschematic
Pole offset is exaggerated by the slider factor; the sidereal rotation angle is not. The frame is mean ecliptic and equinox of date (precession not animated); Moon and Sun are at mean positions.
Zoom×1.0
Texture—
Pinch, scroll or use the slider to zoom (Follow Station keeps north up). Detail streams from an embedded 8192×4096 tile pyramid (≈ 4.9 km/texel at full depth). Clouds are procedural and fade out when zoomed; the night side is brightened when zoomed so terrain stays visible.
Exaggeration×1000
Rotation rate0.004178°/s · 15.0411°/hr
GAST angle—
Since open—
The globe rotates at the true GAST angle. The rotation axis is displaced by nutation (Δψ, Δε) and polar motion (x, y), scaled by the slider. Continents and graticule are visual references. The Moon marker follows its mean orbit.
